Annotate source code with line and branch coverage

Source: R/annotate_coverage.R
annotate_coverage.Rd

Produces plain text showing source lines together with their coverage counts, in a form that is easy to read in a terminal or to paste into a prompt. By default the missed lines are shown with context surrounding lines.

Usage

annotate_coverage(
  x,
  lines = NULL,
  context = 2,
  files = NULL,
  max_lines = getOption("covr.annotate_max_lines", 200)
)

Arguments

x

A coverage object, e.g. from package_coverage() or code_coverage().

lines

A data frame with filename and line columns identifying the lines to show, e.g. the result of zero_coverage() or the lines changed in a pull request. Other columns are ignored. The default is all missed code lines in x, and the lines with a missed branch if branch coverage was measured.

context

Number of lines to show before and after each line in lines. Use Inf to show whole files.

files

Optional character vector of file names (as they appear in the coverage, e.g. "R/foo.R") to restrict the output to.

max_lines

The maximum number of source lines to show, 200 by default (option covr.annotate_max_lines). Whole chunks of lines are added until the next one would go over the limit, but the first chunk is always shown. If anything is left out, the last line says how many of the missed or requested lines in how many files are not shown. Use Inf for no limit.

Value

A character vector of class covr_annotation, with one element per output line. If there is nothing to show it is "No missed lines.".

Details

Each shown line has the line number, a count column and the source. Missed lines are marked !!0, covered code lines show their hit count, and lines without coverage data (blank lines, comments, ...) have an empty count. Non-adjacent chunks are separated by ....

If branch coverage was measured (see covr.branch_coverage), lines with a branch that was not taken are also shown by default, followed by <- not taken: and the labels of their missed branches. Only if and switch() calls that were evaluated count; the others are covered by the missed lines. Such a line keeps its count if it was run.

Examples

source <- "
f <- function(x) {
  if (x) {
    'yes'
  } else {
    'no'
  }
}
"
cov <- code_coverage(source, "f(TRUE)")
annotate_coverage(cov)
#> /tmp/RtmpcMDT40/source.R18657bea0515
#>   4 |    1 |     'yes'
#>   5 |      |   } else {
#>   6 |  !!0 |     'no'
#>   7 |      |   }
#>   8 |      | }
annotate_coverage(cov, context = Inf)
#> /tmp/RtmpcMDT40/source.R18657bea0515
#>   1 |      | 
#>   2 |      | f <- function(x) {
#>   3 |    1 |   if (x) {
#>   4 |    1 |     'yes'
#>   5 |      |   } else {
#>   6 |  !!0 |     'no'
#>   7 |      |   }
#>   8 |      | }
